title: Isandro and the Salt
premise: Orsen Coldharbour, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent twenty years erasing herself in the Thornfell mountains, guarding a covenant she believes is already dead. When a mute child named Isandro arrives at her door speaking the First Tongue—the language that binds the realms—Orsen learns the covenant is not broken but starving, and the child is its living keystone. Hunted by salt-wraiths, a rival order that wants the child's power harvested, and her own buried grief, Orsen must retrace the smugglers' roads to the drowned gate beneath the mountains and speak a new oath. She succeeds only by giving up the memories that made her a swordspeaker, choosing an unknown future with her found family over the identity she has hidden behind.
about_author: Ansel Ishikawa is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fantasy. Their work blends precise landscape writing with quiet, character-driven meditations on memory and belonging.

chapters.title: The Door in the Drift
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A blizzard traps Orsen in her isolated waystation until she finds a child, frost-bitten and silent, at her door. The boy speaks words that make her oath-mark burn—the First Tongue, dead for two centuries. Emotional beat: dread cracking open long-sealed loneliness.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Salt
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Testing Isandro's language against her fragmented oath-training, Orsen confirms he is a keystone—a living anchor of the realm-covenant. She decides to send him away for his own safety. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Wraith Tide
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Salt-wraiths—creatures of the drowned gate—assault the waystation, drawn to Isandro's voice. Orsen speaks her first sword-oath in twenty years and destroys them, but the act broadcasts her location. Emotional beat: the intoxication and terror of reclaiming her power.

chapters.title: The Order of the Quiet Blade
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, rendered through his alien perceptions. Survivors of a rival order arrive offering protection; Orsen recognizes them as harvesters who once butchered her own order. She refuses them. Emotional beat: Isandro's wordless trust in Orsen solidifies into attachment.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Fleeing through smugglers' tunnels, Orsen recalls the fall of her order and her broken oath of silence. Isandro's presence forces memories she has salted away. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as anger.

chapters.title: The Ferryman of Thornfell
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They bargain passage with Vess, a one-eyed ferrywoman who owes Orsen an old debt. Vess becomes an unlikely ally and the first thread of found family. Emotional beat: wary humor thawing into loyalty.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The harvesters ambush the ferry crossing; Isandro, terrified, unconsciously speaks and the river itself rises to defend him. The group escapes but Vess's boat burns. Emotional beat: awe at the child's power, fear of what it will cost him.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Grief
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In a high shepherd's bothy, Orsen begins teaching Isandro common speech while he teaches her fragments of the First Tongue. She learns his village was harvested to leave him orphaned and unguarded. Emotional beat: mourning shared across a language barrier.

chapters.title: The Salt Road South
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The party descends toward the drowned gate, pursued by harvesters and wraiths alike. Orsen realizes the covenant is starving because no oath-speaker has renewed it in generations. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: A City That Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The group passes through the sunken ruin of Aldmere; Isandro reads the First Tongue inscriptions and reveals the gate was not sealed—it was fed, willingly, by oath-speakers of old. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by the dawning price of renewal.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Toll
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess's estranged brother, now a harvester captain, offers her amnesty for Isandro. She refuses, burning her last bridge to her old life. Emotional beat: the ache and freedom of chosen family over blood.

chapters.title: What Orsen Buried
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Captured briefly by harvesters, Orsen is shown her own sealed memories: she once refused to renew the covenant, believing her order's sacrifice was murder, not duty. Emotional beat: identity shattered—was she a coward or a conscience?

chapters.title: The Escape from Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with Isandro interludes. Isandro's spoken grief collapses the harvester stronghold's walls; they flee into the deep roads. Orsen stops treating him as a charge and begins treating him as a person. Emotional beat: fierce, protective love.

chapters.title: The Last Oath-Speaker's Doubt
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the gate's threshold, Orsen confesses her old refusal to Isandro and Vess. Vess's blunt forgiveness, and Isandro's simple trust, force her to confront that hiding was its own betrayal. Emotional beat: humility before forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Price of the Tongue
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro reveals what the inscriptions never said plainly: renewal requires an oath-speaker to surrender the memories that fuel their voice. He offers himself. Orsen refuses to let a child pay. Emotional beat: heartbreak and defiance.

chapters.title: The Harvesters' Gate
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The harvester order arrives in force to seize Isandro at the threshold, led by Orsen's former mentor, who believes harvesting the child will save both realms cheaply. Battle begins. Emotional beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Steel and Salt
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The climactic battle at the drowned gate; Vess holds the causeway at terrible cost while Orsen duels her mentor. Isandro's voice tears the wraith tide apart. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the proof of family.

chapters.title: The Oath Unspoken
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Mortally close to defeat, Orsen understands: the covenant was never meant to be renewed by one speaker, but by many voices bound by love. She begins the oath with Isandro and Vess answering her. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into communion.

chapters.title: What the Water Takes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The covenant accepts the threefold oath, and Orsen's swordspeaker memories—the source of her isolation—dissolve into the gate. The wraith tide stills; the realms breathe again. Emotional beat: grief and release braided together.

chapters.title: A Woman Without a Name
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Waking with gaps where her past was, Orsen must decide who she is without the identity that defined her. Isandro speaks her name in the First Tongue—his first word in it since arrival: not 'Coldharbour,' but 'home.' Emotional beat: rebirth through being known.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's New Road
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The trio rebuilds the waystation as a school for the First Tongue, gathering scattered survivors of Orsen's order. The covenant will need many voices. Emotional beat: quiet hope, the first unguarded laughter.

chapters.title: Isandro and the Salt
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A year later, Isandro writes—or speaks—the story's title into the covenant stone: the salt that preserved the past now preserves a future. Orsen watches, no longer hiding, no longer alone. Emotional beat: belonging earned, memory transformed into legacy.
